subject.title: feat(workspace): lint and auto-fix code fences in markdown at write time

question: Should OpenClaw core normalize workspace Markdown code fences at write time, and if so should it be default auto-fix, warn-only, or an explicit opt-in repair action?
rationale: The requested behavior changes user-authored workspace files, adds configuration/API surface, and prior candidate PRs showed parser correctness risk, so automation cannot safely choose the product default.

options.title: Opt-in diagnostic/fix
options.body: Keep workspace writes verbatim by default and add a parser-backed lint or explicit repair action only after maintainers approve the surface.

options.title: Default write-time auto-fix
options.body: Accept the mutation policy and require a robust CommonMark-aware implementation, config/docs, and upgrade-safe tests before merge.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Decline core write-time Markdown normalization and point users to external markdownlint or workspace tooling instead.

recommendation.title: Opt-in diagnostic/fix
recommendation.body: Keep workspace writes verbatim by default and add a parser-backed lint or explicit repair action only after maintainers approve the surface.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Gateway workspace file API and workspace bootstrap code history point to this area owner signal.
